- **Convergence Requirement:** The approximation relies on the model being converged; otherwise, the residual term in the Hessian is significant [S1].

The claim states that the approximation relies on the model being converged because otherwise, the residual term in the Hessian is significant. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'On a converged 3D-GS model, the ||IG−Igt||1 residual term of Equation 4 approaches zero, causing the second order term (IG(ϕ) − Igt)∇2 G IG in Equation 6 to vanish'. This confirms that the validity of the approximation (where the second term vanishes) depends on the model being converged (residual approaching zero). If not converged, the residual term would not vanish (i.e., would be significant).

The Fisher Sensitivity Score is a pruning metric for 3D Gaussian primitives that estimates the impact of each Gaussian on the L2 reconstruction loss using a block-diagonal approximation of the Hessian [S1].

The claim states that the Fisher Sensitivity Score is a pruning metric for 3D Gaussian primitives that estimates the impact of each Gaussian on the L2 reconstruction loss using a block-diagonal approximation of the Hessian. Source [S1] explicitly defines the L2 loss (Eq. 5), derives its Hessian (Eq. 6), and notes that on a converged model, this approximates the Fisher Information matrix (Eq. 7). It further specifies that the pruning score $U_i$ is based on the log-determinant of a block-diagonal approximation of the Hessian restricted to spatial mean and scaling parameters (Eq. 10 and Section 4.1/4.3). Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
